answer: Each identity claims one stack filter and locks a 70-credit bond. In one sampling pulse, the filter traps soot from its plume; an auditor reweighs it against a reference crystal, then recomputes expected soot from the plume-flow table times pulse length. A shortfall, overclaim, or reused filter burns the bond. The first assay costs 31 credits, the k-th 31+6(k-1), the 1000th 6025; 1000 fake identities pay 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-filter ring fails: two filings from one filter share one soot pattern and burn both bonds. An honest agent pays 31 once, bond returned after audit.
